cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We keep walking past the station. I do this near my old office. Tell me which person we're avoiding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My old boss. He thinks I left for a better job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the facts separate from the story you gave him. I told mine I was writing a novel. What would yours discover?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've been unemployed for six months.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My notebook is still blank. 'Unemployed' isn't an explanation of this route. Is it seeing him, or having to ask him for help?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 uses personal avoidance as bait. A3 corrects the mixture of fact and public story while offering the novel claim; A5 corrects unemployment as an incomplete motive and exposes the blank notebook.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 boss and better-job account cause A3's truth/story distinction. B4 unemployment becomes the basis for A5's more revealing admission and fear-versus-help question.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 offer plausible shame-related details while A shares their own failed claim, keeping B an understandable person rather than merely a source of clues.

heightening.evidence: A5's blank notebook is a more vulnerable truth prompted by B4's six months, used to reach a more specific motive behind the route.

specificity.evidence: A1 station detour, B2 former boss and B4 unemployment locate the avoidance. No unseen map is needed to understand walking past instead of entering.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's correction is pointed, but its admission and question both work on the same motive; no extra joke follows.

coach2.inferred: They know enough of each other's departures for small admissions to open a harder conversation.
coach2.missing: The actual boss's attitude is unknown and is not invented.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate; A5's alternatives are hypotheses offered to B, not facts the reader must assume.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 identifies the person and false impression behind A1's route question.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 uses B2 story to offer a parallel claim and ask for the hidden fact.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 supplies the employment fact requested by A3.
